:::{#def-second-derivative}
#### Second derivative

Let $f$ be a real-valued function of one variable
whose [derivative](calculus.qmd#def-derivative) $f'$ exists
at every point of an [open interval](sets-functions.qmd#def-interval) containing $c$.
If $f'$ is [differentiable](calculus.qmd#def-differentiable) at $c$,
its derivative there, written $f''(c)$ or $\dif{^2 f}{x^2}$,
is the **second derivative** of $f$ at $c$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-second-derivative}
#### The second derivative of $x^3$

For $f(x) = x^3$, $f'(x) = 3x^2$ at every $x$,
and differentiating again gives $f''(x) = 6x$.
So $f''(2) = 12$, $f''(0) = 0$, and $f''(-1) = -6$.

:::
